data.name: Tridha
data.gender_notes: Tridha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Tridevi’, meaning three goddesses, Tridha is a beautiful and powerful name for a baby girl in the Hindu culture. This name is believed to bring the blessings of the three primary goddesses - Lakshmi, Saraswati, and Parvati, symbolizing prosperity, knowledge, and love respectively.
data.spiritual_meaning: Tridha is a divine name, evoking the blessings of the three primary goddesses - Lakshmi, Saraswati, and Parvati. It is believed that a child named Tridha will be blessed with the qualities of these goddesses and will grow up to be prosperous, knowledgeable, and loving.
data.etymology: Tridha belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Three Goddesses.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tridha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Tridha holds immense cultural significance in the Hindu tradition as it is believed to be blessed by the three primary goddesses. It is customary for parents to choose a name with religious or cultural significance, and Tridha is a perfect choice for parents who wish to honor Indian traditions and imbue their child with the qualities of the goddesses.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Tridha has a profound spiritual significance as it evokes the energies of the three powerful goddesses. The name serves as a constant reminder to the child, and those around her, of the importance of prosperity, knowledge, love, and the power of the divine feminine. It is believed that the blessings of these goddesses will protect and empower the child throughout her life, enabling her to overcome any challenges she may face and fulfill her potential.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Tridha symbolizes the three fundamental aspects of life - Truth (Satya), Dharma (Duty), and Artha (Prosperity). It is a reminder for the individual to uphold these principles in their daily life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Tridha is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a princess. The name Tridha carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Tridha was the daughter of King Virata of Hastinapura and was married to Bhima, one of the Pandava brothers.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Tridha continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
